scope_gaps.note: NHS advice is given for insomnia (regular sleep problems); the meta-analysis abstract speaks of sleep after caffeine in general. Neither snapshot recommends reducing the amount of caffeine.
The NHS page is a public patient-information page with a Do/Don't list for self-treatment of insomnia, not a clinical guideline; the 6-hour item sits in one line together with smoking and alcohol.

Abstract only: the population studied and how the 8.8 h was derived are not visible. The sentence states neither. The recommendation is the authors' (the abstract says 'should be consumed') and is tied to avoiding a reduction in total sleep time.
The abstract does not describe how the 8.8 h and 13.2 h figures were derived from the pooled data; it only says the study results provide the guidance.
The abstract does not give the comparator, population, caffeine dose range, confidence interval or heterogeneity for the 45 min; it states only the pooled reduction.
Sentence says 'różnych napojów'; the 13.2 h figure belongs to a pre-workout supplement, not described as a drink in the abstract.
Absence is shown only for the NHS main region (4304 of 4844 characters) and for the abstract; the full article was not available.

notes: Opened only the role file, AGENTS.md, the packet and the two cited snapshots (df5a689db3e18396.txt, b59686537010480d.txt); Grep was run only on those two snapshot paths. The lead source (10.5664/jcsm.3170, fcfee9b228206080.txt) was not opened and was not used as evidence. packet.warnings was empty; both cited snapshots are the expected documents (Gardiner et al. 2023 abstract via Europe PMC, DOI and title match; NHS Insomnia page, main region, reviewed 19 March 2024). No protocol violation. The meta-analysis snapshot is abstract-only, so methods, population and derivation of the hour figures could not be checked. Judgement calls: W praktyce#1 treated as fully backed by the premise that caffeine timing affects sleep (sources do not themselves advise self-observation); the clauses 'nie osobista granica bezpieczeństwa', 'średni wynik nie jest osobistą prognozą' and 'nie zastępuje oceny przyczyn przewlekłych problemów ze snem' were filed as meta_statement (editor's caveats); 'nie godzinę na zegarze' was treated as an absence claim and gets not_checkable because one of its two sources is abstract-only.
